model.name: Work Assignment
model.purpose: Represent the time-bounded occupancy of a role, post or equivalent duty scope by a person or other agent, including the organizational, locational and authorization context of that occupancy, so that an agent can create, inspect and operate assignments independently of the standing position and of the underlying employment or engagement relationship.
model.scope_statement: A work assignment is the reified n-ary relationship in which an agent occupies a role or post for an organization (or comparable host) during a stated interval, optionally constrained by location, service, effort fraction, reporting line and authorization. The model covers identity, classification, composition, state, time, location, authority, constraints, evidence, privacy and interoperability of that occupancy. It does not itself define the person, the position catalogue, the employment contract, a task or work-order, or an information-system permission grant.
in_scope: Identity of a single assignment instance, including master-system identifiers, governed IRIs and Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID values.

Classification of assignment form, including primary occupancy, concurrent occupancy, acting or interim coverage, detail, secondment, time-limited promotion, job-share, volunteer, contractor and unnamed locum occupancy.
Reference to the assigned agent, the occupied post or role, the host organization or unit, and the location or service scope of performance.
Authorization and occupancy intervals, including planned, actual, future-dated, retroactive and non-adjacent periods treated as distinct instances.
Effort fraction, concurrency and exclusivity constraints, including separation-of-duty limits inherited from role policy.
Lifecycle events that create, amend, reassign, temporarily promote, detail, suspend, end, cancel or supersede an occupancy without necessarily changing employment tenure.
Assigning authority, legal or policy basis, evidence artefacts and provenance of assignment acts.
Access, privacy, retention and erasure rules applicable to assignment records as employment-context personal data.
Alignment mappings to W3C ORG Membership and Post occupancy, HL7 FHIR PractitionerRole, Schema.org Role and EmployeeRole, NIST and INCITS RBAC user-role assignment, and US federal personnel actions.
out_of_scope: The standing position, post or job description itself, which belongs to the Position model (WM-ORG-004).
The employment, contractor or volunteer relationship as a whole, which belongs to the Employment relationship model (WM-ORG-005).
Person or agent identity master data, organizational structure, site master data and role or occupation catalogues.
Compensation, payroll, benefits and salary-band catalogues, except where an assignment merely references a remuneration annotation.
Information-system permission grants, sessions and role activation as defined by RBAC, which may be triggered by a work assignment but are not the assignment.
Manufacturing work-order, work-schedule or personnel-class resource assignment under IEC 62264 and ISA-95.
Shift roster, appointment slot and calendar availability as operational schedules, except as optional context on an occupancy.
Patient-scoped care-team membership, competency inventories, qualification licences as master records, and military permanent-change-of-station orders as a dedicated personnel-movement model.

boundary_notes.distinction: A Post or Position exists independently of any incumbent. W3C ORG treats org:Post as a position that may be vacant and org:Membership as the relationship that exists only while an Agent occupies a role. This model records occupancy, not the standing post.

An employment or other engagement may be realized through one or more assignments, including concurrent roles. FHIR states that the represented organization need not be the direct employer of the practitioner. ILO Recommendation No. 198 addresses determination of an employment relationship from facts of work, not occupancy of a named post. Assignment is therefore a realization, not a synonym, of employment.

org:Role denotes the abstract role; org:Membership denotes a specific person playing that role in a specific organization. Schema.org Role likewise qualifies a relationship with startDate, endDate and roleName. This model is the qualified occupancy, not the role concept.

FHIR contrasts PractitionerRole as the general allocation of a practitioner to work places, contact points and services with CareTeam as finer-grained, often patient-scoped functional membership. Patient-specific team slots are out of scope.

boundary_notes.neighbor: NIST and INCITS 359 RBAC user-role assignment
boundary_notes.distinction: Core RBAC defines UA as a many-to-many user-to-role assignment of permissions, plus session activation and static and dynamic separation of duty. That relation assigns system privileges, not organizational occupancy of a post. A work assignment may be a source of truth for later UA provisioning, but the two relations are not the same.

boundary_notes.neighbor: ISA-95 and IEC 62264 personnel resource models
boundary_notes.distinction: ISA-95 Part 2 defines personnel as one of four common resource models exchanged between enterprise and manufacturing operations. That assignment is a production-resource binding to a work definition or schedule, not occupancy of an organizational post.

boundary_notes.neighbor: US federal appointment versus position change
boundary_notes.distinction: 5 CFR 335.101 provides that a position change authorized by section 335.102 does not change competitive status or, with listed exceptions, tenure. Promotion, demotion, reassignment, detail and time-limited promotion are personnel actions on occupancy, not a new employment relationship.

sources.title: The Organization Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative n-ary Membership among Agent, Organization and Role; Post occupancy via holds and heldBy; memberDuring interval; distinction between vacant posts and memberships.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR PractitionerRole Resource

sources.title: Schema.org Role and EmployeeRole
sources.relevance: Qualified relationship pattern with startDate, endDate and roleName; EmployeeRole adds base salary and currency for employee occupancies.

sources.title: Role Based Access Control FAQs and INCITS 359 reference model
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Core RBAC user-role assignment UA, role activation in a session, and static and dynamic separation-of-duty constraints that a work assignment may have to respect when provisioning access.

sources.title: 5 CFR Part 335 Promotion and Internal Placement
sources.version_or_date: eCFR current as of 20 August 2026; Title 5 last amended 14 August 2026
sources.relevance: Federal authority to promote, demote or reassign; time-limited promotions; details to higher-graded positions; 120-day competition threshold; reconstruction records; tenure unchanged by position change.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Attribution, association, generation, invalidation, startedAtTime and endedAtTime, and qualified influence for provenance of assignment records and of assignment-creating activities.

sources.relevance: Confirms personnel as a first-class resource exchanged with equipment, material and physical assets, establishing a sibling manufacturing-assignment boundary rather than organizational occupancy semantics.

sources.title: R198 Employment Relationship Recommendation, 2006
sources.relevance: International instrument on determining an employment relationship from facts of work; used here as a boundary so that assignment of duties is not conflated with the existence of employment.

bundles.name: Assignment identity and kind
bundles.description: How a work assignment is identified, labelled and classified as a distinct occupancy instance rather than as a person, a post or an employment contract.
bundles.rationale: W3C ORG reifies membership; FHIR assigns business identifiers to a role-location occupancy and requires a new instance for each non-adjacent period; Schema.org Role is an intermediate qualifier on a relationship. Identity and kind must be settled before occupancy, time or authority can be operated.

layers.name: Assignment instance identity
layers.description: Master identifiers, IRIs and Dimension-assigned surrogates for one occupancy instance.

findings.name: Assignment instance identity
findings.description: Each occupancy is a distinct identifiable object. FHIR PractitionerRole.identifier holds business identifiers specific to a role or location and notes that the same identifier value may appear on multiple instances for different periods or roles. W3C ORG identifies Membership and Post as resources, typically with URIs. Schema.org identifier may hold UUID or other scheme values. A start date is not an identifier.

questions.text: What authoritative master-system identifier uniquely identifies this occupancy in the governing HR or personnel register?
What governed IRI, and if none exists what UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, identifies this assignment independently of storage format?
Which role-location or registration business identifiers apply to this occupancy, and over which validity interval is each identifier good?
If the same agent later occupies the same role after a gap, is a new assignment instance required rather than reopening the prior identifier?

data_elements.name: Assignment identifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of the occupancy instance in the authoritative register.

data_elements.name: Assignment IRI
data_elements.description: Governed global identifier for the membership or occupancy resource.

data_elements.name: Dimension UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Surrogate assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or IRI identifier is available.

data_elements.name: Role-location business identifiers
data_elements.description: Additional identifiers specific to the role or location, each with optional validity.

artifacts.name: Assignment identity register extract
artifacts.description: Authoritative listing of assignment identifiers, schemes and validity as issued by the personnel or provider register.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the register's assignment or PractitionerRole business identifier; do not use effective date as the identity.

layers.name: Assignment classification
layers.description: Kind of occupancy, including primary versus secondary, acting, detail, secondment, job-share and unnamed locum.

findings.name: Assignment classification
findings.description: ORG distinguishes simple memberOf, annotated Membership and Post occupancy, including ex officio membership. FHIR allows multiple role codes on one occupancy and an empty practitioner for an unnamed hospital role. 5 CFR 335 distinguishes promotion, demotion, reassignment, detail and time-limited promotion. These are classifications of occupancy, not of the person.

questions.text: What kind of occupancy is this, for example primary, concurrent, acting, detail, secondment, time-limited promotion, job-share, volunteer, contractor or unnamed locum?
Is this the agent's primary occupancy, a secondary concurrent occupancy, or an ex officio occupancy derived from another post?
Which role or function codes is the agent authorized to perform under this occupancy?
Does this classification, such as a detail or time-limited promotion beyond 120 days to a higher grade, require competitive procedures under the governing personnel rules?

data_elements.name: Assignment kind
data_elements.description: Coded kind of occupancy drawn from the governing personnel or directory scheme.

data_elements.name: Primacy
data_elements.description: Whether the occupancy is primary, secondary or ex officio.

data_elements.name: Authorized role codes
data_elements.description: Roles the agent may perform for the host under this occupancy.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is coded reference data on the assignment instance; no separate artefact is required beyond the assignment record and any personnel-action notice captured under evidence.

bundles.name: Parties and occupancy targets
bundles.description: The agent who occupies, the post or role occupied, and the host organization, keeping person, post and employment as referenced siblings.
bundles.rationale: ORG Membership is an n-ary relation among member, organization and role; a Post may be held by multiple agents and may exist vacant. FHIR PractitionerRole references practitioner and organization separately and permits an empty practitioner. Schema.org Role intermediates member and organization.

layers.name: Assigned agent
layers.description: Who or what occupies the role, including unnamed and non-person cases that have primary support.

findings.name: Assigned agent
findings.description: ORG Membership.member is a foaf:Agent, covering persons and organizations. FHIR PractitionerRole.practitioner is 0..1 and may be empty for an un-named surgeon at a named hospital. PROV-O distinguishes Person, Organization and SoftwareAgent as agents, but HR occupancy of posts by software agents lacks primary HR-standard support and is recorded as a gap when claimed.

questions.text: Which person or other agent occupies this assignment, and what master identifier is used for that agent?
Is the occupancy an unnamed or pre-allocated role with no designated practitioner, and if so what host and role still identify the slot?
Is the holder an organization or post treated as an agent, as permitted for some government ex officio constructions?
If a software or robotic agent is claimed as occupant, what primary HR or personnel source supports that claim, or is the claim marked as a gap?

data_elements.name: Assigned agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the occupying person or other agent; omitted only for unnamed occupancy.

data_elements.name: Agent type
data_elements.description: Person, organization, or, where evidenced, software agent.

data_elements.name: Unnamed occupancy flag
data_elements.description: True when the occupancy describes a role at an organization without a named practitioner.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The assigned agent is a reference to a sibling identity model; unnamed occupancy is a boolean plus host and role on the assignment record.

layers.name: Occupied post or role
layers.description: Whether occupancy targets a standing post, an abstract role, or both.

findings.name: Occupied post or role
findings.description: ORG Post exists independently of any holder; holds links an agent to a post in an organization and entails Membership when the post has a role. Membership can also be asserted without a Post. Schema.org roleName is the named position or function. Occupancy must state which pattern is used and must not duplicate the post definition.

questions.text: Which standing post or position, if any, is occupied, and is that post currently allowed to have multiple holders?
Which abstract role or named function does the occupant play, whether or not a standing post exists?
Is this occupancy a membership without a standing post, and if so why is a Post representation not used?
Should holding the post entail an org:Membership with the post's role in the host organization?

data_elements.name: Occupied post
data_elements.description: Reference to the standing post or position when occupancy is post-based.

data_elements.name: Played role
data_elements.description: Reference to the abstract role or named function.

data_elements.name: Role name
data_elements.description: Human-readable named position or function filled by the occupant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Post and role are references to sibling catalogue models; the occupancy stores only the binding.

layers.name: Host organization
layers.description: Organization in which the occupancy is exercised, which need not be the employer.

findings.name: Host organization
findings.description: ORG Membership.organization is the organization of membership. FHIR PractitionerRole.organization is where the roles are available and need not be the direct employer. This host is the scope of occupancy, not the employment contracting party.

questions.text: Which organization hosts this occupancy, and is that organization the agent's employer?
Which organizational unit contains the occupied post or membership, if finer than the host organization?
If the occupant is seconded, detailed or supplied by another employer, which home organization remains the employer of record?

data_elements.name: Host organization
data_elements.description: Organization in which the occupancy is exercised.

data_elements.name: Home employer
data_elements.description: Employer of record when different from the host, as in detail or secondment.

data_elements.name: Employment relationship
data_elements.description: Optional reference to the employment or engagement that this occupancy realizes.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Host, home employer and employment relationship are references to sibling organization and employment models.

bundles.name: Scope, location and services
bundles.description: Where and in what functional scope the occupancy is authorized to be exercised.
bundles.rationale: FHIR scopes PractitionerRole by location, specialty, healthcareService and contact. ORG links agents and organizations to Site and basedAt. Schema.org Role does not itself carry place; place remains a sibling concern attached to the occupancy.

layers.name: Location and functional service scope
layers.description: Sites, locations, specialties and services that bound the occupancy.

findings.name: Performance location and services
findings.description: FHIR PractitionerRole.location, specialty, healthcareService, contact, characteristic, communication, availability and endpoint describe where and how the occupant provides services. Distinct instances are required when availability, telecom or other details are not the same across services or locations. ORG basedAt and Site capture organizational location independently of occupancy.

questions.text: At which locations or sites is this occupancy authorized to be performed?
Which specialties and services is the occupant authorized to provide under this occupancy?
What official contact details, languages and technical endpoints belong to this occupancy rather than to the person master record?
If locations, services or telecom differ, must this occupancy be split into multiple assignment instances?

data_elements.name: Authorized locations
data_elements.description: Locations or sites at which the occupancy may be performed.

data_elements.name: Specialties
data_elements.description: Functional specialties practiced under this occupancy.

data_elements.name: Healthcare or business services
data_elements.description: Services provided for the host under this occupancy.

data_elements.name: Occupancy contact details
data_elements.description: Addresses, telecom and endpoints specific to the occupancy.

artifacts.name: Provider or staff directory entry
artifacts.description: Published directory record of the occupancy's locations, services, contacts and endpoints.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by assignment identifier plus host organization; directory publication is a projection, not a second identity.

bundles.name: Time, effort and concurrency
bundles.description: When the occupancy is authorized, how much effort it consumes, and how it coexists with other occupancies.
bundles.rationale: ORG memberDuring uses a time interval. FHIR period is the authorization interval and non-adjacent periods are distinct instances. Schema.org Role uses startDate and endDate. 5 CFR time-limited promotions have a stated limit not exceeding five years unless OPM authorizes longer. Availability calendars are not the occupancy interval.

layers.name: Occupancy and authorization interval
layers.description: Planned, actual and authorization clocks for the occupancy.

findings.name: Occupancy and authorization period
findings.description: FHIR period is the interval during which the person is authorized to act in the role for the organization; revoked authority must still be recorded. ORG memberDuring is optional. Schema.org uses ISO 8601 startDate and endDate. PROV-O records startedAtTime and endedAtTime on activities and generatedAtTime on entities. Event time and ingestion time must be kept distinct, in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

questions.text: During which interval is the occupant authorized to perform the role, including open-ended ends where still authorized?
What are the planned start and end, the actual start and end, and the observation or ingestion times of those facts?
Is the occupancy future-dated, contemporaneous, or retroactive, and what authority supports a retroactive effective time?
Do non-adjacent occupancies of the same role exist, and are they recorded as distinct assignment instances?

data_elements.name: Authorization start
data_elements.description: Inclusive start of authorized occupancy as RFC 3339 date-time.

data_elements.name: Authorization end
data_elements.description: End of authorized occupancy; absent when still open.

data_elements.name: Planned start
data_elements.description: Intended start distinct from actual or recorded event time.

data_elements.name: Actual start
data_elements.description: Event time at which occupancy actually began.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: Observation or system ingestion time of the period facts.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Intervals are intrinsic attributes of the occupancy; they are not separate artefacts. Supporting notices are captured under evidence.

layers.name: Effort fraction and concurrency
layers.description: How much of an agent's capacity an occupancy consumes and whether multiple occupancies may coexist.

findings.name: Effort fraction and concurrency
findings.description: ORG allows a Post to be held by multiple people and a person to hold multiple posts. FHIR states a person may have more than one role. RBAC UA is many-to-many, with session activation of a subset of assigned roles and static and dynamic separation of duty. FTE or effort fraction is widely used in HR practice but is not specified by the fetched primary sources and is marked as an alignment gap when treated as normative.

questions.text: What full-time-equivalent or effort fraction is attributed to this occupancy, and from which local policy does that measure come?
Which other occupancies of the same agent overlap this interval, and is concurrency permitted?
Is the occupied post shared among multiple holders, and what share does this occupancy take?
Which other roles or occupancies are forbidden to the same agent at the same time by static or dynamic separation of duty?

data_elements.name: Effort fraction
data_elements.description: Share of capacity attributed to this occupancy; treat as locally governed unless a primary HR standard is cited.

data_elements.name: Job-share flag
data_elements.description: Whether the post is occupied by multiple holders.

data_elements.name: Overlapping assignments
data_elements.description: Other occupancies of the same agent that overlap this interval.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Effort and concurrency are attributes and references on the occupancy; constraint catalogues are referenced rather than stored as artefacts of this finding.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, state and personnel actions
bundles.description: How an occupancy is created, activated, amended, temporarily altered, ended or cancelled, and how those acts relate to tenure.
bundles.rationale: FHIR active marks whether the record is in current use and is distinct from period. 5 CFR 335 enumerates promote, demote, reassign, detail and time-limited promotion, states that position change does not change tenure, and requires reconstruction records. PROV-O models the creating activity, generation and invalidation of the assignment record.

findings.name: Assignment lifecycle state
findings.description: FHIR active indicates whether the practitioner-role record is in active use; if false, period may still show when it was active, and if period is absent no inference is possible. Meaning if missing is generally active. States such as proposed, approved, suspended or cancelled are operational extensions and must be labelled as profile terms rather than FHIR-native.

questions.text: Is this assignment record in active use, or has it been marked inactive because it was created in error or is no longer to be used?
What governed lifecycle state applies, such as proposed, approved, scheduled, active, suspended, ended, cancelled or superseded?
If active is false or missing, what if anything may be inferred from period about when the occupancy was in force?

data_elements.name: Active flag
data_elements.description: Whether the assignment record is in active use.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle state
data_elements.description: Governed state of the occupancy beyond the FHIR active boolean.

data_elements.name: Inactive reason
data_elements.description: Why the record is not in active use, including created-in-error.

findings.inline_only_rationale: State is inline on the assignment record; transitions are events under personnel actions.

layers.name: Personnel actions and temporary forms
layers.description: Promotion, demotion, reassignment, detail, time-limited promotion, acting coverage and return.

findings.name: Personnel action events
findings.description: 5 CFR 335.102 authorizes agencies to promote, demote or reassign listed employee categories. Section 335.101 states that a position change does not change competitive status or, with listed exceptions, tenure. Section 335.103 requires merit procedures for covered promotions and details over 120 days, permits retroactive temporary promotion when an appropriate authority so determines, and requires a temporary reconstruction record kept for two years or until OPM evaluation. These events create or replace occupancies.

questions.text: Which personnel action created or replaced this occupancy: appointment, promotion, demotion, reassignment, reinstatement, transfer or another governed action?
Did this position change alter competitive status or tenure, or do the 5 CFR 335.101 rules that status and tenure are unchanged apply?
Was competition required, and if not which noncompetitive or discretionary exception was used?
What reconstruction record of ratings, ranking and selection is retained, and until when?

data_elements.name: Personnel action type
data_elements.description: Coded action that created, amended or ended the occupancy.

data_elements.name: Prior assignment
data_elements.description: Occupancy replaced by this action, if any.

data_elements.name: Competition used
data_elements.description: Whether competitive procedures were applied.

artifacts.name: Personnel action notice
artifacts.description: Official notice of promotion, demotion, reassignment or equivalent action, including any reconstruction file.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuer and action or standard-form number from the appointing authority; effective date is an attribute, not the identifier.

findings.name: Temporary, acting, detail and time-limited forms
findings.description: 5 CFR 335.102(f) authorizes time-limited promotions for not more than five years unless OPM authorizes longer, with advance written notice that the employee may be returned at any time to the former or an equivalent position. Details and time-limited promotions over 120 days to higher grades generally require competition, counting prior noncompetitive service in the preceding 12 months. Temporary promotion may become permanent without further competition if originally competed and that possibility was advertised. Acting or interim coverage is a common operational form but is not named as such in the fetched 5 CFR text and must not be claimed as a 5 CFR term.

questions.text: What time limit applies to this temporary promotion, detail or acting occupancy, and was advance written notice given?
May the occupant be returned at any time to the former or an equivalent position, and is that return exempt from adverse-action procedures cited in 5 CFR 335.102(f)?
How many days of noncompetitive higher-grade detail or time-limited promotion have accrued in the preceding 12 months, and is further competition required?
Was the temporary occupancy originally competed with notice that it might become permanent, allowing conversion without further competition?

data_elements.name: Time limit
data_elements.description: Stated limit of a time-limited occupancy.

data_elements.name: Return position
data_elements.description: Position or equivalent grade to which the occupant may be returned.

data_elements.name: Accrued noncompetitive days
data_elements.description: Prior noncompetitive higher-grade service counted toward the 120-day threshold.

artifacts.name: Time-limited promotion or detail notice
artifacts.description: Advance written notice of conditions, time limit, competition requirement and return terms.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuing agency notice number; time limit is an attribute, not identity.

bundles.name: Authority, constraints, evidence and records governance
bundles.description: Who may assign, which constraints bind, what evidence and provenance exist, and how personal data in assignment records is accessed, retained or erased.
bundles.rationale: ORG annotates membership with duration and may reference an employment contract. NIST RBAC supplies SSD and DSD constraints and administrative create-and-delete of user-role assignments. 5 CFR requires merit, recordkeeping and privacy protection. PROV-O attributes records to agents. GDPR Article 88 and ICO employment-records guidance govern processing, retention and erasure in the employment context.

layers.name: Assigning authority and constraints
layers.description: Legal basis, appointing official, eligibility and separation of duty.

findings.name: Assigning authority and legal basis
findings.description: 5 CFR 335.102 vests agency authority to promote, demote or reassign subject to merit programs in 335.103. Candidates must meet OPM minimum qualification standards. GDPR Article 88 allows Member State or collective-agreement rules for processing in recruitment, performance of the employment contract, organization of work and termination. Authority to assign is distinct from authority to employ.

questions.text: Which official or body authorized this occupancy, and under which statute, regulation, collective agreement or delegation?
What lawful basis and, if applicable, Article 88 national or collective rule justifies processing this assignment as employment-context personal data?
Which organization is controller or record owner of the assignment, and who is the operational maintainer of the register?
What minimum qualification, licence or rating-of-record checks were required and what was the outcome?

data_elements.name: Authorizing official
data_elements.description: Agent or body that authorized the occupancy.

data_elements.name: Legal or policy basis
data_elements.description: Citation of the statute, regulation, agreement or delegation used.

data_elements.name: Record controller
data_elements.description: Organization accountable for the assignment record as personal data.

artifacts.name: Delegation instrument or merit promotion plan
artifacts.description: Written agency program or delegation under which the occupancy was authorized.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuing organization and instrument number or plan version.

findings.name: Constraints and separation of duty
findings.description: RBAC static separation of duty constrains user-role assignment; dynamic separation of duty constrains roles activated in a session. Work assignment is not UA, but occupancy may be used as input to UA and must not create forbidden combinations. 5 CFR 335.103 forbids non-merit factors in promotion and placement. Cardinality limits on post holders come from ORG's statement that a post can be held by multiple people, which is permission rather than a universal constraint.

questions.text: Which static separation-of-duty or mutually exclusive role pairs forbid this occupant from holding listed other occupancies?
Which dynamic separation-of-duty rules restrict which of the occupant's roles may be active together in one session or duty period?
What minimum and maximum number of simultaneous holders does the occupied post allow?
Was selection for this occupancy made solely on job-related criteria, excluding the non-merit factors listed in 5 CFR 335.103?

data_elements.name: Static separation-of-duty constraints
data_elements.description: Role pairs or sets that must not be assigned to the same user.

data_elements.name: Dynamic separation-of-duty constraints
data_elements.description: Role sets that must not be simultaneously active.

data_elements.name: Holder cardinality
data_elements.description: Allowed number of simultaneous occupants of the target post.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Constraints are referenced policy objects evaluated against occupancy data; they are not stored as documents of the assignment itself.

layers.name: Evidence, privacy and interoperability
layers.description: Provenance, artefacts, access, retention, erasure and alignment to external occupancy models.

findings.name: Evidence and provenance
findings.description: PROV-O attributes entities to agents, associates activities with agents, records generation and invalidation times, and supports qualified attribution and association. FHIR requires that even revoked authority remain recorded. 5 CFR 335.103 requires reconstruction records of promotion actions and protection of privacy in those records. Assignment evidence is the trail of who created, approved, amended or invalidated the occupancy.

questions.text: Which activity generated this assignment record, which agent was associated with that activity, and to whom is the record attributed?
What notices, contracts, directory entries or reconstruction files evidence this occupancy, and what integrity hash or source identifier do they carry?
If the occupancy or its record was ended or created in error, when was it invalidated, by which activity, and is the historical fact still retained?
What completeness, source reliability and verification status are claimed for this occupancy record?

data_elements.name: Attributed agent
data_elements.description: Agent to whom the assignment record is attributed.

data_elements.name: Generated at
data_elements.description: Event time the assignment record was generated.

data_elements.name: Invalidated at
data_elements.description: Event time the assignment record was invalidated.

data_elements.name: Evidence references
data_elements.description: Supporting artefacts for the occupancy.

artifacts.name: Assignment provenance bundle
artifacts.description: Named set of provenance assertions for creation, approval, amendment and invalidation of the occupancy.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bundle IRI or audit batch identifier; timestamps are attributes.

findings.name: Privacy, retention, access and erasure
findings.description: Assignment records are employment-context personal data. GDPR Article 88 permits more specific national or collective rules for recruitment, contract performance, organization of work and termination, with safeguards for dignity, group transfers and workplace monitoring. ICO guidance states employers should not rely on consent given the imbalance of power, must keep data accurate and no longer than necessary, must meet subject access, and may refuse erasure where a legal obligation such as tax or social-security reporting remains. FHIR security category for PractitionerRole is Individual. 5 CFR 335.103 requires that promotion records protect privacy.

questions.text: Who may read, create, amend or delete this occupancy, and which scopes of the model are visible by default?
How long must this assignment record be retained for personnel reconstruction, tax, social security or litigation, and when does storage limitation require deletion or anonymization?
Has the data subject requested erasure, and which legal-obligation or other Article 17 exceptions require refusal for all or part of the occupancy record?
Which emergency, whistleblowing, occupational-health or official-authority exceptions permit access beyond the default need-to-know rule?

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Governed retention for the assignment record or its reconstruction file.

data_elements.name: Erasure exceptions
data_elements.description: Legal bases to refuse or delay erasure.

data_elements.name: Access policy
data_elements.description: Need-to-know policy identifier for the occupancy.

artifacts.name: Privacy notice and retention schedule
artifacts.description: Worker-facing notice and schedule stating purposes, lawful bases, retention and rights for assignment records.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Controller and notice or schedule version identifier.

findings.name: Interoperability alignments
findings.description: This model aligns to, and does not claim conformance with, W3C org:Membership and org:holds, FHIR PractitionerRole, Schema.org Role and EmployeeRole, RBAC UA, and ISA-95 personnel resources. Conflicts include FHIR's one period per instance versus systems that reopen a row after a gap; ORG's dual Membership and Post patterns; Schema.org EmployeeRole mixing employment and occupancy; RBAC assigning permissions rather than posts; and ISA-95 assigning production resources rather than organizational occupancy.

questions.text: Which external Membership, PractitionerRole, EmployeeRole or UA records correspond to this occupancy, and under which mapping profile?
Which known modelling conflicts apply to this occupancy, such as reopened rows versus new instances, or host-not-employer versus employer-only systems?
What fields must be present to exchange this occupancy with a FHIR, ORG or directory consumer without implying unearned conformance?

data_elements.name: External correspondences
data_elements.description: Mapped identifiers in aligned occupancy models.

data_elements.name: Mapping profile
data_elements.description: Named profile used to project this occupancy to an external model.

data_elements.name: Conflict flags
data_elements.description: Known alignment conflicts applicable to this instance.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Alignments are correspondence metadata on the occupancy; they are not stored as separate exchange documents in this finding.

functions.name: Create assignment
functions.description: Record a new occupancy of a role or post by an agent for a host during a stated interval, without implying a new employment relationship.
preconditions: Host organization exists.
Target post exists or membership-without-post is explicitly chosen.
Agent exists unless unnamed occupancy is allowed.
SSD constraints are evaluated.
effects: A new assignment instance exists with master identifier and provenance.
The standing post, if any, remains a separate resource.
Employment tenure is unchanged unless a sibling employment function is invoked.

functions.name: Activate assignment
functions.description: Mark an approved occupancy as in active use from an actual start time.
preconditions: Assignment is approved or scheduled.
Actual start is recorded in RFC 3339 with offset or Z.
effects: The occupancy is in active use.
Directory or reporting consumers may treat the occupant as incumbent.

functions.name: Amend assignment scope or period
functions.description: Change locations, services, contacts or planned end without replacing the occupancy identity, unless FHIR-style split rules require a new instance.
preconditions: Assignment exists and is not cancelled.
If availability, telecom or services differ across remaining locations, a split is considered.
effects: The same identifier continues unless a split creates related instances.
Historical values remain recoverable from provenance.

functions.name: Reassign or change position
functions.description: End or supersede the current occupancy and create a new occupancy for promotion, demotion or reassignment without changing tenure except as the governing personnel rules provide.
preconditions: Appointing authority is delegated.
Qualification standards are met.
Competition or a listed exception is recorded for covered actions.
effects: Prior occupancy is ended or superseded.
Competitive status and tenure remain unchanged unless a listed exception applies.

functions.name: Establish detail or time-limited promotion
functions.description: Create a time-bounded higher-grade or other temporary occupancy with notice of return terms and 120-day competition accounting.
preconditions: Advance written notice is given, or a nondiscretionary promotion records notice as soon as possible.
Time limit does not exceed five years unless a higher authorization exists.
effects: A temporary occupancy exists alongside or instead of the home occupancy as locally modelled.
Return to the former or equivalent position remains available as specified in the notice.

functions.name: End or cancel assignment
functions.description: Close an occupancy at an actual end, or cancel it before start, while retaining the historical fact of authorization where required.
preconditions: Assignment exists.
If created in error, inactive reason is recorded.
Retention rules are applied before any erasure.
effects: The occupancy is no longer in active use.
The fact that authorization existed remains recorded when required.
RBAC UA provisioning, if any, is a separate downstream effect.

functions.name: Query occupancy at time
functions.description: Determine who occupies a post, which occupancies an agent holds, and which locations and services are in force at a given instant.
inputs: post or agent or location identifier
preconditions: As-of time is an RFC 3339 timestamp.
Query authority covers the requested scope.
effects: Results distinguish active records from historic authorized periods.

functions.name: Evaluate assignment constraints
functions.description: Test proposed or existing occupancy against holder cardinality, overlapping effort, SSD and DSD, and competition thresholds.
preconditions: Constraint catalogues are identified.
Concurrent occupancies of the agent are known.
effects: Create or activate may be blocked until violations are waived or resolved.

composition.purpose: A standing post or position is occupied through one or more scoped assignments; the post may remain vacant and is not identical with any occupancy.
An employment or other engagement may be realized through one or more assignments, including concurrent roles and host organizations that are not the employer.
The occupant is a person or other agent identified in a sibling identity model; unnamed occupancy omits the agent rather than inventing a person.
Host organization, containing unit and optional home employer are sibling organization resources.
Performance locations and organizational sites bound where the occupancy may be exercised.

Align occupancy fields to PractitionerRole identifier, active, period, practitioner, organization, code, specialty, location, healthcareService, contact, availability and endpoint without claiming FHIR conformance.
Align to Membership among member, organization and role, and to holds and heldBy of a Post, including memberDuring.
Align the qualified-relationship pattern using startDate, endDate, roleName and, for employee occupancies, base salary as an annotation only.

composition.target: NIST and INCITS 359 RBAC user-role assignment
composition.purpose: Treat UA, session activation and SSD or DSD as related access-control relations that may be provisioned from occupancy, not as the occupancy itself.

composition.target: ISA-95 and IEC 62264 personnel resource assignment
composition.purpose: Keep manufacturing personnel-class and work-schedule assignment as a sibling industrial model rather than as organizational occupancy.
Mix in generation, invalidation, attribution, association and event versus ingestion times for assignment records.

owner_package_requirements: The owning Dimension must name the authoritative personnel or provider register that issues master assignment identifiers.
The owning package must declare whether occupancy is post-based, membership-without-post, or both, and must not silently collapse those patterns.
The owning package must separate host organization from employer of record and must state when an employment relationship is required.
The owning package must publish retention, access and erasure rules for assignment records as employment-context personal data.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint assignment IRIs under the adopting Dimension's assignment register. Prefer the authoritative HR or provider-register identifier; then a governed IRI such as an org:Membership URI; then a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID. Do not use an effective date as an identifier. Optional alignments may cite http://www.w3.org/ns/org#Membership or a FHIR PractitionerRole identifier without treating those IRIs as native identity.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical occupancy is one assignment instance per continuous authorization interval; non-adjacent periods of the same agent in the same role are separate instances.
Person, post, employment, location and permission-grant identifiers remain references, not duplicated masters.
Timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; planned, actual, effective, generated and ingested clocks are not collapsed.
Unnamed occupancy is represented by omitting the agent, not by a placeholder person.
patch_rules: Patches that change host, post or agent identity supersede the occupancy and mint a new assignment identifier.
Patches that only amend contacts, services or planned end on an otherwise identical scope may update in place with provenance.
If locations or telecom diverge, split into related instances rather than overloading one occupancy.
Created-in-error records are inactivated and invalidated, not silently rewritten.
compatibility_rules: Do not claim FHIR, ORG, Schema.org, INCITS 359 or ISA-95 conformance from alignment maps alone.
Consumers must accept occupancies that have a role but no post, and posts that have no current holder.
RBAC UA must not be inferred solely from occupancy unless a documented provisioning profile says so.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system assignment identifier from the governing HR, personnel or provider register.
Governed global identifier or IRI for the membership or occupancy resource.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master identifier or IRI exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event time and observation or ingestion time separately using RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts such as personnel-action notices use issuer code plus the issuer's action or form number; effective date, grade and post title are attributes and must not be concatenated as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artefact carries an integrity hash or source identifier and is attributed to the generating activity and agent; directory projections are not alternative masters.

policies: Occupancy is need-to-know personal data in the employment or professional-directory context and is processed under a documented lawful basis, not by default on worker consent.
Merit, qualification and separation-of-duty constraints are evaluated before activation of a covered occupancy, and reconstruction records are retained for the governed period.
Historical authorized occupancies are retained even after revocation or ending until retention expires; erasure is applied only where no legal-obligation or other exception remains.

read: Authorized HR operations, managers in the reporting line, the occupant for their own record, auditors and privacy officers may read according to scope.
Directory consumers may read only fields published to a directory profile.
As-of queries must state the instant used.
create: Only an appointing authority or delegated registrar may create an occupancy.
Create evaluates SSD, holder cardinality and, where applicable, competition thresholds.
Create always writes provenance of the generating activity.
update: Scope and period amendments require the same authority class as create unless a documented local amendment delegation exists.
Identity of agent, host or post is not updated in place; a superseding occupancy is created.
Active flag and lifecycle state changes are audited.
delete: Hard delete is forbidden while reconstruction, tax, social-security or litigation retention applies.
Operational delete is inactivation plus invalidation with reason.
Erasure of residual personal data follows the privacy process after retention expiry or a valid erasure request.

roles.name: Appointing authority
responsibilities: Authorize promotion, demotion, reassignment, detail and time-limited occupancy within delegated limits.
Issue or cause issue of written notices and personnel-action evidence.

roles.name: Assignment registrar
responsibilities: Maintain canonical occupancy records, splits and supersessions.
Ensure reconstruction files can rebuild a covered action.

roles.name: Line manager
responsibilities: Propose occupancy, acting coverage and return from temporary occupancy.
Confirm actual start and end event times.

roles.name: Assigned agent
responsibilities: Exercise subject-access and, where applicable, rectification or erasure rights against the assignment record.

roles.name: Records and privacy officer
responsibilities: Apply retention, access and erasure rules to occupancy records.
Handle employment-context data-subject requests and exceptions.

roles.name: Constraint and access steward
responsibilities: Maintain SSD, DSD and competition-threshold evaluations.
Keep RBAC UA provisioning aligned with, but distinct from, occupancy.

access.default_rule: Deny by default; grant need-to-know read of occupancy to the occupant, appointing authority, registrar and current reporting line, with narrower directory fields to public or partner consumers.
exceptions: Official-authority, occupational-health, whistleblowing, safety and legally compelled disclosure may open additional fields with time-bounded grants and audit.
Unnamed locum occupancy may be published at host and role granularity without a person identifier.
audit_requirements: Every create, identity-affecting update, activation, end, cancel, access exception and erasure decision is attributed to an agent and activity with event time and ingestion time.
Promotion reconstruction files remain auditable for two years or until the governing evaluation period lapses.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
Read the assignment specification and identity rules before any occupancy payload.
Read process descriptions for create, activate, reassign, detail, end and erasure before mutating records.
Treat JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB as projections of the same occupancy semantics.

coverage.claim: This model covers the reified, time-bounded occupancy of a role or post by an agent, including identity, kind, host versus employer, location and service scope, authorization interval, lifecycle personnel actions, authority, separation-of-duty constraints, evidence, privacy and alignments to W3C ORG, FHIR PractitionerRole, Schema.org Role, US 5 CFR personnel actions and RBAC UA as a related but distinct relation. It does not claim a single global HR information model or metaphysical completeness.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier, IRI and Dimension UUID or ULID are specified; FHIR role-location business identifiers and the new-instance-after-gap rule are included.
Active versus period, personnel actions, time-limited promotion, detail, return and invalidation are covered from FHIR and 5 CFR 335.
Agent, post, role, host, home employer, employment relationship, locations, services and concurrent occupancies are modelled as references.
Authorization period, planned versus actual clocks, future-dated and retroactive occupancy, and non-adjacent periods as distinct instances are covered.
PROV-O generation, attribution, association, invalidation and event versus ingestion time are mixed in.
Controller versus registrar versus appointing authority are distinguished; host is not assumed to be employer.
Qualification standards, merit-only selection, SSD and DSD evaluation, and competition thresholds are included.
Need-to-know default, directory projection, FHIR Individual security category and official-authority exceptions are specified.
5 CFR reconstruction retention, ICO storage limitation and erasure with legal-obligation exceptions are covered; hard delete while retention applies is forbidden.
Alignments and conflicts for ORG, FHIR, Schema.org, RBAC and ISA-95 are recorded without conformance claims.
Primary, concurrent, unnamed, membership-without-post, detail and time-limited promotion are classified; acting is flagged as operational language not named in 5 CFR.
FTE and effort fraction are widely used in HRIS practice but were not found as a normative element in the fetched primary sources.
Home-versus-host employer is modelled, but EU Posted Workers and detailed secondment instruments were not retrieved as primary text.
PROV-O SoftwareAgent exists, but no fetched HR or personnel standard treats a software agent as occupant of a work assignment.

known_omissions: ISO 30400:2022 HR terminology is paywalled and was not retrieved; job, position and assignment terms from that standard are not claimed.
HR Open Standards position-assignment schemas were not retrieved as public technical text.
IEC 62264 object-model attributes for personnel class assignment remain behind the ISA and IEC paywall; only the public ISA-95 overview was used.
ILO Recommendation No. 198 full instrument text did not load from NORMLEX in this run; only the official landing page is cited.
Military permanent-change-of-station and assignment-order systems were not fetched.
Shift roster, cost-center accounting splits and compensation as a function of occupancy lack primary support here.
National labour-dispatch and agency-worker regimes beyond the host-versus-employer distinction are not specified.
conflicts: FHIR requires a new PractitionerRole instance for non-adjacent periods; many HRIS products reopen a single assignment row after a gap.
W3C ORG offers both Membership and Post occupancy; profiles that force one pattern will not round-trip the other.
Schema.org EmployeeRole mixes occupancy qualifiers with employment salary, overlapping WM-ORG-005.
NIST RBAC UA assigns permissions, not posts; provisioning occupancy into UA is a policy choice, not an identity of relations.
5 CFR 335 is United States federal competitive-service law and is not a global personnel-action code.
ISA-95 personnel assignment is a manufacturing resource binding and must not be treated as organizational occupancy.
regional_assumptions: Merit promotion, 120-day detail accounting and five-year time-limited promotion limits are United States federal (5 CFR Part 335) and apply only where that law is the appointing regime.
GDPR Article 88 and ICO employment-records guidance apply to EU and UK processing; other privacy regimes may impose different retention and erasure outcomes.
Unnamed locum occupancy is drawn from FHIR healthcare practice and may be uncommon in general HRIS.
Secondment, labour dispatch and posted-worker constructions are jurisdiction-specific and are represented here only as host-versus-home employer.
adversarial_checks: If a consumer treats assignment identifier as the person identifier, unnamed locum and job-share occupancies become corrupt; agent and assignment identities were kept separate.
If a consumer equates host organization with employer, contractor, secondment and FHIR non-employer hosts are misclassified; host-is-employer is explicit.
If a consumer infers RBAC permissions from occupancy alone, SSD-safe posts can still yield over-privilege; UA is aligned, not composed as identity.
If a consumer reuses one assignment across a gap, FHIR period semantics and audit reconstruction fail; instance-per-gap is required.
If acting coverage is claimed as a 5 CFR term, the claim is false; acting is marked as operational language without that primary label.
If FTE is treated as internationally standardized, the claim is false; effort fraction is a documented gap.
